The proposed solution is correct.

1. **Upper bound**: A forbidden configuration $\{n, p_1 n, \dots, p_r n\}$ corresponds in the exponent lattice $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^r$ to a translated star $a + V$, where $V = \{0, e_1, \dots, e_r\}$. In the simplex $T_X$, there are $C = \Psi_S(X/\max p_i) = (1 - o(1))\Psi_S(X)$ such stars. Any subset $A \subseteq T_X$ avoiding all stars has complement $B = T_X \setminus A$ which must intersect every star. Since each point $v \in \mathbb{Z}^r$ belongs to at most $r+1$ stars (as the base or as one of the $r$ endpoints), double-counting edge-vertex incidences gives $(r+1)|B| \ge C$, leading to $|A| \le \left(\frac{r}{r+1} + o(1)\right)\Psi_S(X)$.

2. **Lower bound**: Setting $\phi(a) = \sum_{i=1}^r i a_i \pmod{r+1}$ maps $V$ bijectively onto $\mathbb{Z}/(r+1)\mathbb{Z}$. Thus, every translate $a+V$ contains exactly one element with $\phi(a+v) \equiv 0 \pmod{r+1}$. Removing the sublattice $\ker \phi$ (which has index $r+1$ and asymptotic density $\frac{1}{r+1}$) leaves a star-free subset of asymptotic density $\frac{r}{r+1}$.

Both bounds match, establishing $\lim_{X\to\infty} \frac{F_S(X)}{\Psi_S(X)} = \frac{r}{r+1}$.
